[accessed 2026-09-20]. jw.org in Chiphimbi (Phimbi, language code phm): 'Mboni za Yahova' site with online Bible 'Baibolo' (New World Translation books Genesis/Genezesi.. Chivumbuluso, ca. 50 books, text + MP3 audio + PDF), Watchtower study editions, brochures, tracts, songs and videos in Chiphimbi.https://www.jw.org/phm/
sources.note: Nothing: religious texts, audio and video in Phimbi only; no orthography guide, pronunciation note or grammatical description was found on the site (library sections: Baibolo, magazini, mabukhu, Brochures-and-Booklets, Tracts, nyimbo, Mavidiyo, Guidelines, Indexes). Value for the catalog: (a) proof that a standardized written Phimbi with long audio-aligned texts exists openly (usable for acoustic/aligned stress measurement later), (b) the vernacular glossonym Chiphimbi.

sources.citation: Zahran, Aron & Rozenn Guérois. 2026. Functions and grammaticalization pathways of *ngà 'like, as' in the Lower Zambezi. In: Bantu 11 - 11th International Conference on Bantu Languages (Ghent University), Book of Abstracts (version), pp. 230-231. Ghent: BantUGent. [contains example (4) 'Phimbi N48, Mozambique (Fieldnotes 2024)']
sources.note: No phonology content. The abstract is morphosyntactic (grammaticalization of *ngà); its single Phimbi datum is a glossed sentence printed WITHOUT tone or length marks: 'Ngati unganiɓetseɾe, ningakuphase cakudya' (ngati u-nga-ni-ɓetseɾ-e ni-nga-kuphas-e ca-kudya, COND SP2-POT-OP1SG-help-SBJV SP1SG-POT-OP2SG-give-SBJV 7-food) 'If you can help me, I can give you food' (p. 231). Nothing on stress, accent or tone for Phimbi (neighbouring Chikunda and Doma examples do carry tone marks).

sources.citation: Zahran, Aron, Maud Devos & Rozenn Guérois. 2026. The development of negative 'have' auxiliaries in the Bantu languages of the Middle and Lower Zambezi. Nordic Journal of African Studies 35(1): 136-187 (with Appendix). doi:10.53228/r3qmd434.
sources.note: marks only: fieldwork examples carry surface tone marks (fn. 2 'We present the fieldwork examples as spoken, including surface tones'), e.g. 'Pano tina kamú:tí kaɗí:kí komwe tiná:ko', 'Ndiɾi názo má:ɾí' (H tones and penultimate vowel length visible); no statement about the tone system or stress.
